subtype: Approach: finding out what each plant needs [Thinking]
passage: Note from Nilesh at the plant nursery. A boy of about ten, Ojas, came in on Saturday and asked what each of his two seedlings needs. I told him chilli wants plenty of sun and mint does better in the shade. He had forgotten his notebook, so he wrote it on his palm. "So chilli by the window and mint next to the wall," he said. I nodded. On Tuesday he came back with a photo of both pots in their places and asked if that was right. It was. - Nilesh

qa.q: Where did Ojas write down what he learned?
qa.a: He wrote it on his palm.

qa.q: What was Ojas feeling when he came back with the photo on Tuesday?
qa.a: Eager and a little unsure whether he was right, but proud enough to show his work.

qa.q: What else could Ojas do to check the plants get the right light, and why?
qa.a: He could watch the pots over several days and move them if the leaves look pale or burnt, because plants show what they need.

qa.q: How does Nilesh see Ojas's return visit?
qa.a: Nilesh is pleased and encouraging, since Nilesh confirms it was right and notes the boy's interest.

grounding: A boy asks a nursery worker what each plant needs and places his pots by the window and the wall accordingly.
